en: The Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Auspicious Lord of Obstacles (Śrī Vighneśvara)

The Leader, the King of Obstacles, the Son of Gaurī, the Lord of the Gaṇas; the Eldest Brother of Skanda, the Imperishable, the Pure, the Skillful, the Overseer, and the Beloved of the Twice-born. || 1 ||

The destroyer of the pride of Agni, the bestower of Indra’s glory, the giver of eloquence, the imperishable one, the bestower of all perfections, whose body is Śarva, and who is dear to Śarvarī. || 2 ||
Śiva, the creator of all, the god worshipped by many, whose nature is everything, who is dear to those of pure intellect, peaceful, a celibate student, and elephant-faced. || 3 ||
The son of the two mothers, the sage worthy of praise, the destroyer of obstacles for his devotees; he who has one tusk and four arms, the skillful one endowed with power. || 4 ||
Lambodara, Śūrpakarṇa, Hara, the supreme knower of Brahman, Kāla, the lord of the planets, the lover, and he whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire. || 5 ||
Holding a noose and a goad, he is fierce, beyond the qualities of nature, and stainless; he is untainted, self-perfected, and his lotus feet are worshipped by the perfected ones.

He who is attached to the citron fruit, the bestower of boons, the eternal, the creator; he who is dear to the twice-born, free from fear, the wielder of the mace, the wielder of the discus, and the bearer of the sugarcane bow.

Śrīdoja, whose hand holds a blue lotus, the Lord of Śrī, delighted by hymns of praise; the shatterer of the mountain of the Kula, the one with matted hair, the destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age. || 8 ||
He whose crest-jewel is the moon is lovely, the remover of sins, and composed; he bestows prosperity upon those who take refuge in him, is gentle, and grants the desires of his devotees. || 9 ||

He is peaceful, the bestower of the bliss of liberation, whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss; he is a man of knowledge, endowed with compassion, self-controlled, and free from hatred toward Brahman. ||10||
The bestower of fear upon the negligent Daityas, Śrīkaṇṭha, the Lord of the wise, worshipped by Rāma, the Ordainer, who has the king of serpents as his sacred thread. ||11||
Thick-necked, the self-creator, supremely fond of the sound of the Sāman chants; thick-lipped, the leader, steadfast, the Lord of Speech, the bestower of perfection. || 12 ||
He who loves dūrvā grass and bilva leaves, whose form is unmanifest yet possesses a wondrous form, and whose mind is eager for dalliance on the lap of the daughter of the mountain king.
The essence of the nectar of his own exquisite beauty, he has conquered the form of the God of Love; he is the support of the entire world, the master of illusion, whose vehicle is a mouse. (14)
Joyful, contented, and serene in soul, the bestower of all accomplishments [praised] the omnipresent Lord Vighneśvara with these one hundred and eight names.
Śaṅkara praised his son who was intent on destroying Tripura; whoever worships Siddhivināyaka with devotion by means of this very [prayer], [shall attain success]. 16.
By means of dūrvā grass blades, bilva leaves, flowers, sandalwood, or unbroken rice grains, one attains all desires and is liberated from all obstacles.
